summary: The lecture covers Earth's interior structure using direct and indirect sources, focusing on seismology. It details seismic wave types (P, S, Love, Rayleigh), their properties, earthquake causes, measurement scales, shadow zones, and India's seismic zoning.
points: Direct sources: deep drilling (Kola Peninsula 12 km), surface rocks, volcanic eruptions
Indirect sources: temperature/pressure variations, meteorites, gravitational anomalies, magnetic field, seismic activity (most important)
P-waves: fastest, travel through solid/liquid/gas, longitudinal, vibrate parallel to propagation
S-waves: travel only through solids, transverse, vibrate perpendicular to propagation
Love waves: horizontal side-to-side motion only; Rayleigh waves: rolling elliptical motion (vertical + horizontal)
Focus/hypocenter: earthquake origin point inside Earth; Epicenter: point directly above focus on surface
Richter scale measures magnitude (energy released); Mercalli scale measures intensity (damage/effects)
Shadow zones: areas where seismographs cannot detect P or S waves due to refraction at liquid outer core
India's seismic zones: Zone II (low), III (moderate), IV (high), V (very high damage risk)
Earthquake causes: plate tectonics (destructive/constructive/conservative boundaries), volcanic activity, rockfall, mining

check.q: Which seismic wave type travels only through solid medium?
